meta.title: EU Disclosure Atlas: insider trades across Europe
meta.description: Open, unified data on insider trading and short selling across European markets, published by national regulators under MAR and the Short Selling Regulation. Live, pseudonymized, research-grade.

search.hint: ↑ ↓ to move · Enter to open · Esc to close

footer.privacy: A research and transparency project. Natural persons appear only as pseudonymous ids.
footer.sources: Sources: Finansinspektionen (FI), data processed and re-used free of charge with attribution · ECB euro reference rates.

home.kicker: Insider trades · short positions · 30 regulators, one dataset
home.title: Europe’s insider trades, in one live, open dataset.
home.lead: EU law makes managers’ trades and large short positions public, but they are scattered across about thirty national regulators, in PDFs, spreadsheets and portals. The Atlas collects them, puts them in one schema and replaces every natural person with a pseudonym.

architecture.metaDescription: How the EU Disclosure Atlas is built: event-driven lakehouse, versioned data, REST, SSE and MCP.
architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.lead: An event-driven lakehouse behind a cache-friendly API. New filings flow from regulators to your screen in minutes, and every number can be reproduced from a versioned snapshot.

website.why: Search-friendly company pages in four languages, streaming, caches invalidated by data commits

explorer.why: Millions of rows queried in the browser, linked views without a server

api.why: One schema from ingestion to the generated TypeScript client

engine.why: Snapshots, time travel and a change feed on files and SQL

orchestration.why: Partitioned assets, backfills, data-quality checks, lineage

events.why: Replayable events from the change feed, retry and dead-letter topics

services.why: Each bounded context scales and fails on its own

platform.why: GitOps, preview environments, autoscaling on lag

security.why: OIDC with passkeys, edge policies, signed supply chain

ai.why: Extraction fallback, natural-language questions, agent access, all evaluated

observability.why: SLOs as code with burn-rate alerts and runbooks

principles.p1: The lake is the system of record; caches, events and search are rebuildable projections.
principles.p2: Every read is pinned to a data snapshot, so answers are consistent, cacheable and citable.
principles.p3: Components react to events, not to polling.
principles.p4: The website uses the public API: no private shortcuts.
principles.p5: Each language where it is strongest: Python for data, TypeScript for the web.
principles.p6: Natural persons are pseudonyms everywhere outside the private raw layer.
